# Kyoto 4-Day Romantic Slow-Travel Plan

A relaxed Kyoto itinerary for **2 adults** from **2026-11-12 to 2026-11-15**, built around temples, local food, and easy walking. I’m assuming **mid-range lodging**, mostly public transit/taxis, and enough flexibility for one rainy day without overpacking the schedule.

## Day-by-Day Kyoto Itinerary

### Day 1: Higashiyama Welcome Walk
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/geo-alt.svg
- Morning: Arrive, check in, and take a slow stroll through **Gion** and **Hanamikoji**.
- Afternoon: Visit **Kennin-ji** or **Kodai-ji**, then continue to **Maruyama Park** for an easy scenic walk.
Media: Image=https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/f/f8/A199_Japan_Kyoto_Maruyama_Park_Gion_Ar%C3%A9a_%284764445344%29.jpg Alt=Afternoon: Visit **Kennin-ji** or **Kodai-ji**, then continue to **Maruyama Park** for an easy scenic walk, Kyoto, Japan
- Dinner: Kaiseki-lite, yuba, or a cozy tofu set meal near **Gion**.

Action: [Button: Map Day 1](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=Gion+Kyoto)

### Day 2: Temple Classics and Riverside Time
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/building.svg
- Morning: Start early at **Kiyomizu-dera** before the crowds.
- Afternoon: Walk downhill through the preserved lanes of **Sannenzaka** and **Ninenzaka**, then visit **Yasaka Shrine**.
- Dinner: Casual local dinner in **Pontocho** or around **Kawaramachi**.

Action: [Button: Map Day 2](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=Kiyomizu-dera+Kyoto)

### Day 3: Arashiyama Nature + Temple Day
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/tree.svg
- Morning: Go to **Arashiyama** early for the bamboo grove and a riverside walk.
- Afternoon: Choose one main temple, such as **Tenryu-ji**, then relax with tea or a boat/river pause if the weather is good.
- Dinner: Return to central Kyoto for a quiet izakaya or soba dinner.

Action: [Button: Map Day 3](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=Arashiyama+Kyoto)

### Day 4: North Kyoto and Departure Day
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/compass.svg
- Morning: Visit **Kinkaku-ji** or **Ryoan-ji** depending on your pace and departure time.
- Afternoon: Keep this flexible for souvenir shopping, a final coffee, or a short temple revisit near your hotel.
- Dinner: If you have time before leaving, do one last easy dinner near Kyoto Station or your lodging area.

Action: [Button: Map Day 4](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=Kinkaku-ji+Kyoto)

## Budget Split for JPY 180,000

| Category | Planned Amount | Share | Notes |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| Lodging | JPY 88,000 | 49% | 3 nights, comfortable mid-range hotel or ryokan-style stay |
| Food | JPY 42,000 | 23% | Breakfasts, lunches, dinners, snacks, and tea breaks |
| Transit | JPY 18,000 | 10% | Subway/bus passes, occasional taxi for comfort |
| Activities | JPY 22,000 | 12% | Temple entry fees, gardens, tea experience, small extras |
| Buffer | JPY 10,000 | 6% | Rainy-day taxi, extra dessert, or last-minute adjustment |

### Spending Guidance
- **Lodging target:** JPY **22,000–30,000 per night** for a relaxed couple-friendly stay.
- **Food target:** JPY **10,000–14,000 per day** for two, including one nicer dinner.
- **Transit target:** Keep walking-heavy days and use taxis selectively to stay comfortable.
- **Activity target:** Kyoto temple admissions are usually modest, so you can afford a few paid stops without pressure.

## Rain Backup Plan

### Best Indoor Swaps
- Replace **Arashiyama** with **Kyoto Railway Museum** or **Kyoto National Museum**.
- Swap temple walking for **Nishiki Market**, covered shopping arcades, and tea stops.
Media: Image=https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/e/e5/A_store_at_Nishiki_market%2C_Kyoto%2C_Japan.jpg Alt=Swap temple walking for **Nishiki Market**, covered shopping arcades, and tea stops, Kyoto, Japan
- Add a long lunch at a traditional restaurant, then do **craft shopping** or a **sake tasting** session.

### Rain-Friendly Day Flow
- Morning: One indoor museum or market.
- Afternoon: Tea house, department store food halls, or a covered arcade walk.
- Evening: Early dinner and an onsen or hotel rest if available.

### Good Rain Pairings
- **Kiyomizu-dera area** → museum + café + pottery shopping
- **Arashiyama** → train ride + indoor temple hall + lunch
- **Central Kyoto** → Nishiki Market + department stores + izakaya dinner
